verified_facts: Docker gives a plain container net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start = 0 (ran: docker run --rm python:3.11-slim-bookworm cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_unprivileged_port_start -> 0). The decoy ran as uid 10001 with --cap-drop ALL, --read-only and no-new-privileges and still bound ports 21/23/80. The compose file sets the sysctl explicitly anyway.

The decoy never starts a connection: a tcpdump in the decoy's network namespace showed 4 SYNs from the client, 4 SYN-ACKs from the decoy, 0 SYN-only packets from the decoy and 0 UDP (DNS) packets from it. The unit test wraps socket.socket.connect and connect_ex, and the only recorded connect is the test client's own connection to the decoy port. asyncio's sock_connect goes through socket.connect, so the hook does see asyncio connections.

Docker macvlan docs (raw.githubusercontent.com/docker/docs/main/content/manuals/engine/network/drivers/macvlan.md, lines 40-52) say the networking equipment must handle promiscuous mode (several MAC addresses on one interface), and that 'Containers attached to a macvlan network cannot communicate with the host directly, this is a restriction in the Linux kernel'. docs.docker.com is blocked by the egress proxy, so I read the upstream source file instead.
docker compose (v5.3.1) config fails with the custom message when a ${VAR:?msg} value is missing, and resolves the file when the values are set (run above).
The unit tests also pass on Python 3.13.5 inside zeek/zeek:9.0.0 with ../deps313 (22 passed). The full unit suite on the host is 791 passed, 1 skipped.

decoy.log has no route to the console yet. The decoy writes /data/decoy.log in its own volume (maxguard-decoy-data), but nothing ships it into an analysis log folder. Options: the live sensor shipper / POST /api/ingest accepts a decoy.log in the upload, or the decoy gets a small shipper. The normalizer also does not read decoy.log yet (EVENT_KEYS already allows source 'decoy'). This needs a decision from Jaiden or Jakub. I did not touch pipeline.py, live.py or shipper.py.

The spec says 'the first 64 bytes received as hex' without a key name. I used first_bytes_hex. Each decoy.log line also has a 'service' key (telnet/ftp/http), which the rule uses as Finding.protocol. Line keys: ts, service, src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port, first_bytes_hex. decoy.log has no uid/community_id, so Evidence.uid is ''. Adding community_id later would let the dashboard join decoy lines to Zeek/Suricata records.

FIO-07 wording: Step 4 says a device 'using' a new service, but 'What you just did' says 'a device that suddenly offers a new service'. I built 'uses': the device is the src_ip (originator) of a conn event, keyed on (dst_port, proto, service). Detecting new services a device OFFERS would be keyed on dst_ip and needs a separate decision. Please make the doc text consistent.

Baseline choices beyond the spec, to cut false positives (please confirm or fix in the docs): (a) only kind=='conn' events are counted, because http/ssl/eve describe the same connection again; (b) Zeek service 'ftp-data' is ignored, because its port changes on every transfer; (c) an event with service '' counts as known when the device already used the same port and proto; (d) devices with no baseline entry are skipped, not flagged, because flagging them would flood on every new device.

Shape of the stateful contract: context = {'baseline': <dict from build_baseline>, 'learning_ends': <epoch float>}. Events with ts < learning_ends never give a finding. Baseline shape: {ip: {'peers': int, 'services': [[port, proto, service], ...]}}, with devices and services sorted. I added run_stateful(log_dir, context), which runs STATEFUL_RULES in sorted order and calls base.merge(). Nothing calls it yet: pipeline.py needs a hook, plus somewhere to store the baseline (StateStore?) and the learning_ends setting. That is the lead's or Jaiden's decision. The rule calls normalize(log_dir, sensor_id='') internally; sensor_id does not affect any field it uses.

STATEFUL_RULES and @stateful_rule live in maxguard/rules/baseline.py, as instructed. I think they belong in maxguard/rules/base.py next to RULES so that future stateful rules do not import a specific rule module. stateful_rule() refuses IDs already in RULES, but base.rule() does not check STATEFUL_RULES, so a later @rule with a stateful ID would not be caught. If the registry moves to base.py, both checks can be symmetric.

docker/decoy-compose.yaml requires MAXGUARD_DECOY_SUBNET, MAXGUARD_DECOY_GATEWAY and MAXGUARD_DECOY_IP with no defaults (${VAR:?msg}), because a default IP could clash with a real device. Only the parent has a default (eth0), as the task asked. So a bare 'docker compose -f docker/decoy-compose.yaml config' (FIO-06 step 3) prints a clear error, and the docs should show the command with the three variables set (see docs-draft/decoy-baseline-notes.md).
Finding has no confidence field, so the 'high-confidence' wording in the FIO-06 Goal is not represented in the data. Severity is critical.
doc_notes:
Decoy (FIO-06):
- service.py is pure standard library (asyncio). Telnet and FTP send their banner first because those servers speak first. HTTP waits for the request, then sends a page titled 'Printer admin'.
- Every connection writes one JSON line (sort_keys) to decoy.log in a finally block, so garbage, silence (timeout) or an early hang-up still gets logged. The contact itself is the evidence.
- Limits: it reads at most 1024 bytes, logs at most 64 bytes as hex, and waits at most 5 s (MAXGUARD_DECOY_TIMEOUT).
- The clock is injectable (clock=...), which lets tests check exact ts values. Port 0 in tests picks a free port, so no root is needed.
- functools.partial passes service, log path, timeout and clock to the handler; asyncio adds reader and writer.
- The 'never connects out' test wraps socket.socket.connect/connect_ex with monkeypatch and asserts the only connect is the test client's own.

decoy.contact rule:
- One finding per decoy.log line, severity critical, source 'decoy'. Evidence = ids.evidence('decoy.log', line), so record_id is the hash of the line and the AI can cite it.
- merge() counts repeats per (src, dst, port).
- To use it before approval: `from maxguard.rules.decoy import decoy_contact`.

Compose:
- macvlan gives the decoy its own MAC and IP on the LAN.
- The parent must be the console's normal wired NIC, never the sensor capture port.
- The host cannot reach its own macvlan containers (a Linux kernel restriction, per the Docker docs), so test from a laptop.
- Hardening: read_only, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, and the image's non-root user. The sysctl net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0 lets that user bind 21/23/80. Docker already defaults it to 0 in containers (verified); it is set explicitly so the setup does not depend on that default.
- The bridge-network proof in the notes uses the same flags.

Baselines (FIO-07):
- build_baseline(events) uses only conn events. Device = src_ip. Output: {ip: {'peers': n, 'services': [[port, proto, service], ...]}}, sorted and JSON-ready.
- JSON turns tuples into lists, so the rule converts them back (known_services) and works on a json.loads copy (tested).
- The rule takes (log_dir, context) and never reads the clock or the disk for its history; same logs plus same context give the same findings (tested with to_dict twice).
- Test fixture logic: the lab captures all come from 172.18.0.3 to 172.18.0.2, each on one service. The plain_http and clean_tls13 captures are the learning set. Telnet (port 23) is the new service. learning_ends 1791250000 comes before every lab capture.

Gotcha: `pkill -f <pattern>` inside a Bash tool call can kill the calling shell itself (exit 144). Do not use it with patterns that match your own command line.
